title: Building Agents at Cloud Scale — Antje Barth, AWS
talk_summary: AWS argues for model-driven agents built with the Strands SDK, MCP tools, and remote MCP servers on Lambda, with a dice-server demo. Most content is AWS product framing, but the tool-retrieval and remote-MCP patterns are copyable.

takeaways.what_they_do: They store descriptions of a very large tool catalog in a knowledge base and retrieve only the most relevant tools into the model context for the task.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we put the descriptions of those tools in a knowledge base and use the retrieve tool

takeaways.what_they_do: They decouple MCP servers from local stdio by deploying them as Lambda/streamable-HTTP services behind an MCP gateway.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You put your Lambda functions as you would have before behind an MCP gateway

takeaways.technique: Per-request MCP authorization and session isolation
takeaways.what_they_do: They put an authorizer in front of remote MCP and store session data separately so tool calls are authenticated and session-scoped.
Their SDK provides prebuilt support for graph-based workflows or swarms of subagents rather than only free-form agent delegation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: pre-built tools to implement multi- aent workflows whether it's graph-based workflows or a swarm of sub aents
